literal: For merit he was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the South and enfeoffed Earl of Guangwu.
idiomatic: For merit he was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the South and enfeoffed Earl of Guangwu.

literal: Soon afterward Liang invaded Feiliang; an edict ordered Ying to lead a host of a hundred thousand to attack; wherever he went he was to act as circumstances required.
idiomatic: Soon afterward Liang invaded Feiliang; an edict ordered Ying to lead a hundred thousand men to attack; wherever he went he was to act as circumstances required.

literal: Ying memorialized the timing of events and thereupon broke Yinling, beheading twenty-five Liang generals and more than five thousand heads of captives.
idiomatic: Ying memorialized the timing of events, broke Yinling, beheaded twenty-five Liang generals, and took more than five thousand heads.

literal: He again repeatedly defeated Liang armies at Liangcheng, beheading forty-two of their detached generals; killed, captured, and drowned came to nearly fifty thousand.
idiomatic: He again repeatedly defeated Liang armies at Liangcheng, beheading forty-two detached generals; killed, captured, and drowned came to nearly fifty thousand.

literal: Liang Central Army Grand General Prince of Linchuan Xiao Hong, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Yan, and five other great generals fled east along the Huai.
idiomatic: Liang central-army grand general Prince of Linchuan Xiao Hong, left vice director Liu Yan, and five other great generals fled east along the Huai.

literal: In all they took forty myriads of grain.
idiomatic: In all they took four hundred thousand piculs of grain.

literal: Ying pursued to Matou; the Matou garrison commandant of Liang entrusted the city and fled; he then besieged Zhongli.
idiomatic: Ying pursued to Matou; the Matou garrison commandant entrusted the city and fled; he then besieged Zhongli.

literal: An edict said the army had been out long and ordered Ying to have the mind of shaking the troops loose.
idiomatic: An edict said the army had been out long and ordered Ying to withdraw the host.

literal: Ying memorialized: "The term runs to the end of the second month and the beginning of the third; victory is sure by principle.
idiomatic: Ying memorialized, "The term runs to late second month and early third month; victory is sure by principle.

literal: But from the first of this month rain has joined day after day—one may say heaven goes against men's wish.
idiomatic: But from the first of this month rain has joined day after day—heaven goes against men's wish.

literal: Yet when the king's army moves, its action is not easy to change; one must not, because of a little delay, raise dissent.
idiomatic: Yet when the king's army moves, its action is not easy to change; one must not, for a little delay, raise dissent.

literal: I wish the court would especially open a far-reaching plan, grant a little more breadth, lend days and months, and not let the work of moving a mountain stop halfway."
idiomatic: I wish the court would open a far-reaching plan, grant a little breadth, lend days and months, and not let the work of moving a mountain stop halfway."

literal: By the fourth month the water swelled and broke the bridge; Ying and the generals fled in disorder; of soldiers drowned, one or two in ten.
idiomatic: By the fourth month the water swelled and broke the bridge; Ying and the generals fled in disorder; one or two soldiers in ten drowned.

literal: Ying reached Yang Province, sent an envoy to deliver his tally and seals of office, sable tail, cicada insignia, and ribbon of rank; an edict ordered them handed to the keeper of regalia.
idiomatic: Ying reached Yang Province and sent an envoy to deliver his tally, seals, sable tail, cicada insignia, and ribbon of rank; an edict ordered them handed to the keeper of regalia.

literal: The relevant offices memorialized that Ying's calculations failed in plan and impeached him for death.
idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized that Ying's calculations failed and impeached him for death.

literal: An edict pardoned him to death and made him a commoner.
idiomatic: An edict pardoned him from death and made him a commoner.

literal: Later when Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled, Ying's princely enfeoffment was restored; he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, acting Eastern Campaign General, and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Later when Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled, Ying's princely enfeoffment was restored; he was made bearer of the staff of authority, acting eastern campaign general, and commander-in-chief of Ji military affairs.

literal: Before Ying set out, Ji Province was already pacified.
idiomatic: Before Ying set out, Ji was already pacified.

literal: At the time the middle attendant of Ying Province, Supervisor Rongzu, secretly led Liang troops; they responded from Yiyang; garrisons of the Three Passes all held their cities and surrendered to Liang.
idiomatic: At the time Ying middle attendant Supervisor Rongzu secretly led Liang troops; Yiyang responded; garrisons of the Three Passes all held their cities and surrendered to Liang.

literal: Governor of Ying Lou Yue shut the city and held it.
idiomatic: Governor of Ying Lou Yue shut the city and held it.

literal: Men of Xianbi, Bai Zaosheng and others, killed Governor of Yu Sima Yue and held the south of the city in rebellion.
idiomatic: Men of Xianbi, Bai Zaosheng and others, killed Governor of Yu Sima Yue and held the south of the city in rebellion.

literal: Liang General Qi Gou'er led a host to hold Xianbi.
idiomatic: Liang general Qi Gou'er led a host to hold Xianbi.

literal: Yue's son Shang had married Princess Huayang; both were seized as hostages.
idiomatic: Yue's son Shang had married Princess Huayang; both were seized as hostages.

literal: An edict made Ying Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all Southern Campaign military affairs, and acting Southern Campaign General; he set out from Runan.
idiomatic: An edict made Ying bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of southern campaign military affairs, and acting southern campaign general; he set out from Runan.

literal: The emperor, because Xing Luan had repeatedly defeated Zaosheng, ordered Ying south to Yiyang.
idiomatic: The emperor, because Xing Luan had repeatedly defeated Zaosheng, ordered Ying south to Yiyang.

literal: Ying because his troops were few repeatedly memorialized asking for reinforcements; the emperor did not permit.
idiomatic: Ying, his troops being few, repeatedly memorialized for reinforcements; the emperor did not permit.

literal: Yet Ying on his own authority joined Xing Luan in dividing troops to attack Xianbi together, captured it, then led the army south.
idiomatic: Yet Ying on his own authority joined Xing Luan in dividing troops to attack Xianbi, captured it, then led the army south.

literal: Having halted at Yiyang, he was about to take the Three Passes.
idiomatic: Having halted at Yiyang, he was about to take the Three Passes.

literal: Ying calculated: "The three passes depend on one another like left and right hands; if one pass is taken, the other two need not wait for attack to be settled.
idiomatic: Ying calculated, "The three passes depend on one another like left and right hands; capture one pass and the other two need not wait for attack to be settled.

literal: Hard attack is not as good as easy; the eastern pass is easy to attack—you should first take it, as Huang Shigong said: battle like wind rising, attack like a river breaking its banks."
idiomatic: Hard attack is not as good as easy; the eastern pass is easy—you should first take it, as Huang Shigong said: battle like wind rising, attack like a river breaking its banks."

literal: Ying feared they would combine strength in the east; he therefore sent Chief Clerk Li Hua with five detachments toward the western pass to divide their military momentum, while he himself directed the host toward the eastern pass.
idiomatic: Ying feared they would combine in the east; he sent Chief Clerk Li Hua with five detachments toward the western pass to divide their strength, while he directed the host toward the eastern pass.

literal: It was indeed as Ying had calculated.
idiomatic: It was indeed as Ying had calculated.

literal: In all they captured six great generals, twenty detached generals, seven thousand soldiers, forty myriads of grain, and military stores in full measure.
idiomatic: In all they captured six great generals, twenty detached generals, seven thousand soldiers, four hundred thousand piculs of grain, and military stores in full measure.

literal: On return to court he was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: On return to court he was made vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: He died; posthumously made Duke of the Secretariat; his posthumous title was Xianwu.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously made duke of the Secretariat, posthumous title Xianwu.

literal: Ying's son Xi, courtesy name Zhenxing, loved learning and was handsome and bright, had literary talent, and his fame resounded in the age.
idiomatic: Ying's son Xi, courtesy name Zhenxing, loved learning, was handsome and bright, had literary talent, and his fame resounded in the age.

literal: Yet he was frivolous and restless; Ying deeply feared he was not a man to preserve the house and often wished to depose him and establish the fourth son Lue.
idiomatic: Yet he was frivolous and restless; Ying deeply feared he was not a man to preserve the house and often wished to depose him and establish the fourth son Lue.

literal: Lue firmly begged and only then did he stop.
idiomatic: Lue firmly begged and only then did he stop.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Imperial Household.
idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to director of the imperial household.

literal: At the time the commander of the guards Yu Zhong held power.
idiomatic: At the time Commander of the Guards Yu Zhong held power.

literal: Xi was Zhong's son-in-law; therefore within the year he was suddenly promoted.
idiomatic: Xi was Zhong's son-in-law; therefore within the year he was suddenly promoted.

literal: Later he was made Governor of Xiang Province.
idiomatic: He was later made governor of Xiang.

literal: Xi took office in the seventh month; that day great wind and cold rain struck; more than twenty froze to death, and several tens of donkeys and horses.
idiomatic: Xi took office in the seventh month; that day great wind and cold rain struck; more than twenty froze to death, and several tens of donkeys and horses.

literal: Xi heard of his grandfather's earlier affair and hated it in his heart.
idiomatic: Xi heard of his grandfather's earlier affair and hated it in his heart.

literal: Again maggots were born in his courtyard.
idiomatic: Again maggots were born in his courtyard.

literal: Earlier, Xi and his brothers had all been favored by Prince of Qinghe Yi; when Liu Teng and Yuan Cha cut off the two palaces and forged an edict to kill Yi, Xi thereupon raised troops to punish them.
idiomatic: Earlier, Xi and his brothers had all been favored by Prince of Qinghe Yi; when Liu Teng and Yuan Cha cut off the two palaces and forged an edict to kill Yi, Xi raised troops to punish them.

literal: Ten days after Xi raised troops, his chief clerk Liu Yuanzhang, vice director You Jing, and Administrator of Wei Commandery Li Xiaoyi seized Xi and placed him in a high tower, together with his sons and younger brothers.
idiomatic: Ten days after Xi raised troops, his chief clerk Liu Yuanzhang, vice director You Jing, and Wei commandery administrator Li Xiaoyi seized Xi and placed him in a high tower, together with his sons and younger brothers.

literal: Cha sent Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Tong to behead him in the streets of Ye and send the head to the capital.
idiomatic: Cha sent left assistant director Lu Tong to behead him in the streets of Ye and send the head to the capital.

literal: At first Xi's consort, Lady Yu, knowing Xi would surely fail, did not follow his plans; from the first she wept without cease, until Xi's death.
idiomatic: At first Xi's consort Lady Yu, knowing he would surely fail, did not follow his plans; from the first she wept without cease until his death.

literal: Xi was a frontier prince and moreover had literary learning; his air was very high.
idiomatic: Xi was a frontier prince and moreover had literary learning; his bearing was very high.

literal: When he first took Ye as his garrison, learned friends and men of talent—Yuan Fan, Li Yanzhi, Li Shenjun, the Wang Song brothers, Pei Jingxian, and others—all saw him off at the River Bridge and composed poems in farewell.
idiomatic: When he first garrisoned Ye, learned friends Yuan Fan, Li Yanzhi, Li Shenjun, the Wang Song brothers, Pei Jingxian, and others all saw him off at the River Bridge and composed farewell poems.

literal: When he was about to die he again wrote to old acquaintances, regretting that his will was not fulfilled.
idiomatic: When he was about to die he again wrote to old acquaintances, regretting that his will was not fulfilled.

literal: Men of the time prized him.
idiomatic: Men of the time prized him.

literal: Also, before Prince of Rencheng Cheng died, Xi dreamed someone told him: "Rencheng is about to die; two hundred days after his death you too will not escape.
idiomatic: Also, before Prince of Rencheng Cheng died, Xi dreamed someone told him, "Rencheng is about to die; two hundred days after his death you too will not escape.

literal: If you do not believe it, try looking at Rencheng's house."
idiomatic: If you do not believe it, try looking at Rencheng's house."

literal: In the dream Xi looked back at Rencheng's residence; the walls on four sides collapsed; not one piece of wall remained.
idiomatic: In the dream Xi looked back at Rencheng's residence; walls on four sides collapsed; not one piece remained.

literal: Xi hated it; waking, he told those close to him.
idiomatic: Xi hated it; waking, he told those close to him.

literal: When Xi died it was indeed as in the dream.
idiomatic: When Xi died it was indeed as in the dream.

literal: Xi's three brothers each followed Ying on campaign; in the army they were greedy and violent; sometimes in welcoming surrender and pursuing the routed they would cut down the innocent and add many heads to the merit rolls.
idiomatic: Xi's three brothers each followed Ying on campaign; in the army they were greedy and violent; sometimes in welcoming surrender and pursuing the routed they cut down the innocent and inflated head counts on the merit rolls.

literal: Again, when Yu Zhong slandered Guo Zuo and Pei Zhi, Zhong's mind had not yet settled on killing them; because Xi urged and encouraged him, they reached the extreme penalty—men of the age considered it a wrongful death.
idiomatic: Again, when Yu Zhong slandered Guo Zuo and Pei Zhi, Zhong's mind had not yet settled on killing them; Xi urged and encouraged him until they reached the extreme penalty—men of the age considered it wrongful death.

literal: When Xi's calamity came, those who understood thought there was retribution.
idiomatic: When Xi's calamity came, those who understood thought there was retribution.

literal: When the Empress Dowager restored the government, he was posthumously made Grand Duke of the Secretariat; his posthumous title was Prince Wenzhuang.
idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager restored the government, he was posthumously made grand duke of the Secretariat, posthumous title Prince Wenzhuang.

literal: Xi's younger brother Lue, courtesy name Juanxing, held the office of Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Lue, courtesy name Juanxing, held the office of gentleman attendant of the yellow gate.

literal: When Xi failed, Lue fled in secret and entrusted himself to an old acquaintance, Interior Minister of Henei Sima Shibin.
idiomatic: When Xi failed, Lue fled in secret and entrusted himself to an old acquaintance, interior minister of Henei Sima Shibin.

literal: Shibin made a reed raft; at night he and Lue crossed the Meng Ford together and went to the house of Li Faguang of Tunliu in Shangdang.
idiomatic: Shibin made a reed raft; at night he and Lue crossed the Meng Ford and went to Li Faguang's house in Tunliu, Shangdang.

literal: Faguang by nature honored faith and righteousness; he rejoiced and received him.
idiomatic: Faguang honored faith and righteousness by nature; he rejoiced and received him.

literal: Lue's old acquaintance Diao Shuang was then Governor of Xihe; Lue again went to him.
idiomatic: Lue's old acquaintance Diao Shuang was then governor of Xihe; Lue went to him again.

literal: He stayed more than a year; Shuang then had his nephew Chang escort Lue to slip away to the south of the Yangtze.
idiomatic: He stayed more than a year; Shuang then had his nephew Chang escort Lue to slip away south of the Yangtze.

literal: Emperor Wu of Liang treated him with great courtesy and respect, enfeoffed him Prince of Zhongshan, and made him Governor of Xuancheng.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang treated him with great courtesy, enfeoffed him Prince of Zhongshan, and made him governor of Xuancheng.

literal: Soon afterward Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Faseng held the south of the city in rebellion; Liang then made Lue Grand Commander-in-Chief and ordered him to Pengcheng to receive and entice the newly submitting.
idiomatic: Soon afterward Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Faseng held the south of the city in rebellion; Liang made Lue grand commander-in-chief and ordered him to Pengcheng to receive the newly submitting.

literal: Presently Lue was summoned back together with Faseng.
idiomatic: Presently Lue was summoned back together with Faseng.

literal: Though Lue was in Jiangnan, because of his family's calamity he wept morning and night; his person was as if in mourning.
idiomatic: Though Lue was in Jiangnan, because of his family's calamity he wept morning and night; his person was as if in mourning.

literal: He also hated Faseng's person; speaking with Faseng he never once smiled.
idiomatic: He also hated Faseng's person; speaking with Faseng he never once smiled.

literal: Liang again made Lue Governor of Heng Province; he did not go.
idiomatic: Liang again made him governor of Heng; he did not go.

literal: It happened that his Prince of Yuzhang Zong returned to the state with the city; Zong's chief clerk Jiang Ge, Marshal Zu Huanheng, and five thousand soldiers were all taken captive.
idiomatic: It happened that his Prince of Yuzhang Zong returned to the state with the city; Zong's chief clerk Jiang Ge, marshal Zu Huanheng, and five thousand soldiers were all taken captive.

literal: Emperor Ming ordered the relevant offices to send Ge and the rest back south; thereby they summoned Lue, and Liang then sent him off with full ceremony.
idiomatic: Emperor Ming ordered the relevant offices to send Ge and the rest back south; thereby they summoned Lue, and Liang sent him off with full ceremony.

literal: Emperor Ming ordered Director of the Imperial Household Diao Shuang to meet and comfort him at the border; he made Lue Attendant-in-Ordinary and Prince of Yiyang.
idiomatic: Emperor Ming ordered Director of the Imperial Household Diao Shuang to meet and comfort him at the border; he made Lue attendant-in-ordinary and Prince of Yiyang.

literal: On reaching Shiren Post Pavilion, an edict ordered kinsmen of the imperial clan, inside and outside officials who knew him before, to welcome him in the near suburbs.
idiomatic: On reaching Shiren Post Pavilion, an edict ordered imperial kinsmen and inside and outside officials who knew him to welcome him in the near suburbs.

literal: His marshal Shibin was made Gentleman-in-Attendance; Chief Gentleman of the Direct Attendance; Li Faguang was made magistrate of his native county; Diao Chang was made Administrator of Dongping; Diao Shuang was made Governor of Western Yan Province.
idiomatic: His marshal Shibin was made gentleman-in-attendance and chief gentleman of the direct attendance; Li Faguang magistrate of his native county; Diao Chang administrator of Dongping; Diao Shuang governor of Western Yan.

literal: Every place where Lue ate one meal or lodged one night was not without reward.
idiomatic: Every place where Lue ate one meal or lodged one night was rewarded.

literal: Soon he was changed to Prince of Dongping; later he was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Soon he was changed to Prince of Dongping; later he was made director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: The Empress Dowager greatly favored and trusted him; the trust shown him was nearly equal to Yuan Hui's.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager greatly favored and trusted him; the trust shown him nearly equaled Yuan Hui's.

literal: At the time the realm had many affairs; military and civil matters were myriad.
idiomatic: At the time the realm had many affairs; military and civil matters were myriad.

literal: Lue kept to constancy and preserved himself; he had no other benefit—only a compliant minister.
idiomatic: Lue kept to constancy and preserved himself; he had no other benefit—only a compliant minister.

literal: Erzhu Rong was Lue's uncle by marriage; Lue had always looked down on him lightly.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong was Lue's uncle by marriage; Lue had always looked down on him lightly.

literal: Lue again sided with Zheng Yan and Xu He; Rong harbored resentment on both counts.
idiomatic: Lue again sided with Zheng Yan and Xu He; Rong harbored resentment on both counts.

literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, Lue was killed at Heyin.
idiomatic: When Rong entered Luoyang, Lue was killed at Heyin.

literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian and Duke of Works; his posthumous title was Wenzhen.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand guardian and duke of works, posthumous title Wenzhen.

literal: Ying's younger brother Yi held the office of General of the Shanshan Garrison.
idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Yi held the office of general of the Shanshan garrison.

literal: In the garrison he was greedy and violent; the relevant offices impeached him; he fled and escaped punishment and died.
idiomatic: In the garrison he was greedy and violent; the relevant offices impeached him; he fled, escaped punishment, and died.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign, because he was Erzhu Rong's wife's elder brother, he was posthumously made Grand Duke of the Secretariat and Prince of Fufeng.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign, because he was Erzhu Rong's wife's elder brother, he was posthumously made grand duke of the Secretariat and Prince of Fufeng.

literal: His son Su was enfeoffed Prince of Lu Commandery.
idiomatic: His son Su was enfeoffed Prince of Lu.

literal: Su's younger brother Ye, courtesy name Huaxing, childhood name Penzi.
idiomatic: Su's younger brother Ye, courtesy name Huaxing, childhood name Penzi.

literal: By nature he was frivolous and restless and had physical strength.
idiomatic: By nature he was frivolous and restless and had physical strength.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign he was enfeoffed Prince of Changgang.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign he was enfeoffed Prince of Changgang.

literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong and the others set up Ye as ruler; the era name was Jianming.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong and the others set up Ye as ruler; the era name was Jianming.

literal: Presently he was deposed by Shilong.
idiomatic: Presently Shilong deposed him.

literal: When Emperor Jiemin was established, he was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai.
idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin was established, he was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was killed.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was killed.

literal: Prince of Chengyang Changshou was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing and held the office of Grand General of the Woye Garrison; he had a very great reputation for martial prowess.
idiomatic: Prince of Chengyang Changshou was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing and held grand general of the Woye garrison; he had a very great reputation for martial prowess.
